newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania Dacia Felix bank says saw 1996 profit.
newsitem.headline: Romania Dacia Felix bank says saw 1996 profit.

text.p: Romania's troubled private bank Dacia Felix SA had a 33.2 billion lei profit last year after a 642.2 billion 1995 loss, its shareholders' meeting was told on Friday.
Dacia Felix, once a fast-growing bank now struggling with bad debts of some $200 million, was stripped of its banking licence this week on grounds of a deteriorated financial position.

On Thursday, a court in the central Romanian city of Cluj, site of the bank's headquarters, suspended the central bank (BNR) order withdrawing Dacia Felix's operating licence. The order was halted until May 21 under legal proceedings launched by Dacia Felix against BNR.
The bank's interim president Ioan Minecan told the shareholders meeting in Cluj that last year's revenues amounted to 1.24 trillion lei, with spending at about 1.2 trillion.
Minecan said Dacia had still 1.88 trillion lei in debts, the bulk of them to the BNR, but declined to comment on the posible future of the bank.
Dacia Felix has been awaiting a decision by another Cluj court on its fate after the BNR last year lodged a case asking legal authorities to decide on liquidation or reorganisation.
A recovery plan drawn up by the bank provides for foreign capital injection, which must be approved by the BNR.

This week, the BNR also lifted the banking licence of Romanian private bank Renasterea Creditului Romanesc Credit Bank SA, which also contested the move and awaits a Bucharest court to decide on its future on May 8.
Not a single bank has been declared bankrupt in Romania. The country now has 40 commercial banks, created under market reforms launched since the 1989 fall of communism. ($=7,092 lei)
